| [QUESTION-366](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-366.md) | Does an inquiry need the record of its own development to know its object, as Simondon's method and its organization-studies readers hold, or only to revise its conclusions, which is what the record has shown? | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024, p. 1366), quoting Simondon, hold that research "consists in following the being in its genesis, in accomplishing the genesis of thought at the same time as the genesis of the object", and Bencherki and Iliadis (proposition 4) that knowledge of an entity "should reflect on the way that knowledge itself has individuated".
